::: {.unit unit="lp-breacher"}
The breacher carries demolition charges for walls and turrets. Against units the charges do little, and a breacher alone dies quickly. Send breachers in behind troopers and aim them at the pillboxes first.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-trooper"}
The trooper is your basic soldier: heavy armor and a submachine gun, and the cheapest unit on the command link. Troopers beat raiders, scouts and Shotgunners and lose to long-range lasers, so send them in numbers. Only a powered barracks heals them.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-rocket-trooper"}
The rocket trooper's rockets are made for armor and fliers; against troopers plain rockets are no better than a submachine gun, but explosive ones burst among them. It takes more of the command link than a trooper and outranges a Railgun tank's rail cannon. Keep rocket troopers behind your troopers against infantry, and in front against tanks and drones.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-gun-buggy"}
The gun buggy is a car with an autocannon, and the fastest unit you have. Its explosive rounds break up infantry, buggies and drones and do little to a tank's armor. Set a defending beacon's squad with a few of them and they reach the attack first. It rearms with piercing rounds or better, never firearm magazines.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-flame-trooper"}
The flame trooper has the most damage of your infantry, and only the breacher has a shorter range. It burns biter swarms and bunched squads quickly but does little to vehicles, and nearly everything outranges it. Lead with it against Synthexis and keep it at the back against Kessler-Hayashi.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-battle-tank"}
The battle tank fires a slow, heavy shell. It takes the longest to train and the most bandwidth. Its shell is made for buildings, so it is the tool for a walled camp and a poor one against crowds unless it fires explosive shells. Keep troopers with it.
:::
